abstract: Video images converted from films show unnatural reproduction of movement. To correct this, it is necessary to utilize a motion compensation technique that has already been employed for television standards conversion. We modified an existing high-definition television (HDTV) standards converter by adding the necessary functions for motion-compensated film-to-video conversion. To test the practicality of the modified converter, we detected motion vectors on it by using the video signals of images already converted from film by a telecine. Then we interpolated the images using the detected motion vectors to compensate for movement. The result was less unnatural movement and better quality moving images with respect to film-to-video conversion.

authors.bio: Hajime Sonehara joined the NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories in 1989. He is a member of IEICE of Japan.

authors.bio: Yukio Sugiura received his B.E. degree in electrical engineering from Tokyo Denki University in 1963 and Ph.D. degree in engineering from the University of Tokyo in 1995. He joined the Science and Technical Research Laboratories of NHK in 1958. A senior research engineer at the Advanced Television Systems Research Division, he was engaged in research on application of laser technology to optical communication systems, film recording, and telecine. He is currently engaged in research on advanced television systems. He is a member of the Institute of Television Engineers of Japan, the Optical Society of Japan, and Motion Picture and Television Engineering Society of Japan.

authors.bio: Hiroshi Hirabayashi is deputy director of the Planning and Analysis Division Broadcasting Satellite Department of the Telecommunications Advancement Organization of Japan (TAO), in control of the broadcasting satellites. He received his B.E. degree in electronic engineering from Osaka University in 1980 and joined the NHK that same year. From 1983 to 1995, while working at the NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories, he took part in the research and development of the laser beam film recorder, laser telecine, and the HDTV standards converter. Since 1995, he has been on loan to the TAO.
